name: Text similarity never ships anything
rule: A title or text match between a request and a commit/PR is never enough by itself to call something shipped; without an explicit link it prints as a candidate to confirm, not a fact.
why: kill-criterion-1 runs found explicit links 95% correct vs. title text matching 9% correct, 68% wrong (pm/decisions.md). canwe.mjs's bestFind() now exposes whether a matrix-row match came from an explicit ref or only title similarity, and a text-only claim prints as "candidate — confirm".

name: Explicit links only, never inferred
rule: A PR/commit only counts as tied to a decision, request, or issue when there is an explicit reference (closing keyword, #N, issue timeline/comment cross-reference) — never a guess from wording.
why: recent.mjs and shipped-links.mjs tie every PR to its decision via refs.mjs on title+body, explicit refs only, "no tie" otherwise (pm/log.md line 418).

name: Closing references only from the same repo
rule: A closing/linking reference only counts when it comes from the same repository as the issue or PR being checked; a fork's closing reference is ignored.
why: shipped-links.mjs restricts GitHub's own closingIssuesReferences and keyword matches to same-repo, by construction (skill/tools/shipped-links.mjs lines 67, 73); pm/log.md logs 73/74 closed together.

name: The integration branch is detected, not assumed
rule: Where work actually merges is detected from the repo's own merged-PR history (or sources.json's integrationBranch override), never assumed to be the default branch.
why: integration-branch.mjs looks at the branch most merged PRs target; wired into collect-status.mjs, backfill-history.mjs, recent.mjs and shipped-links.mjs (pm/log.md line 305).

name: Tiny samples are hidden, not shown low
rule: A rate, median, or calibration score built on fewer than minN rows (default 10) is withheld and shown as "too few to say" instead of being printed as a low or misleading number.
why: thresholds.mjs's minN (default 10) gates score.mjs's calibration section and scoreboard.mjs's rate/median display; scoreboard.mjs says "too few to say" below that count.

name: An incomplete shipped count is withheld, not shown low
rule: A headline shipped count is only shown once every explicit link kind (PR body keywords, #N mentions, issue timeline/comment cross-references) has actually been counted for that run; otherwise it is not shown at all.
why: Internal request 83, informed by the comprehension-check reading in pm/decisions.md: readers distrusted a "4 shipped" headline contradicted by its own footnote. shipped-record.mjs and scoreboard.mjs withhold the count unless the full link check ran (pm/log.md line 406).

name: A comment-only commit doesn't ship a decision
rule: A commit that only touches comments or non-code lines does not count as shipping a decision, even if it explicitly references that decision.
why: N1 (pm/waves.md line 13): 'The record is right' — done criteria include 'comment-only commits don't ship' as part of the explicit-link record's hand-checked rules (30-row hand-check sample, 3.3% wrong).

name: The code wins when a document claim conflicts with it
rule: When answering "can we do this," a claim from a decision doc or request is checked against the code at the integration ref; if they disagree, the code's evidence is what gets reported.
why: canwe.mjs (post blind-test-v2 rewrite, internal request 95's fix cycle): the question's rarest terms are searched in the code first ("In the code (read this first)"), before decision-doc text; see skill/test/canwe-code.test.mjs header comment.

name: Never rules are pattern-only, language-independent
rule: The owner's "never" rules are matched as plain regex patterns against added lines, not by any language- or framework-specific logic, so they work for a product in any language.
why: never-check.mjs's own header: reads sources.json's preread.never as "the owner's own regex patterns: pattern-only, so a product in any language works" (skill/tools/never-check.mjs lines 1-3).

name: A deliberately-off feature is not "not built yet"
rule: When a decision or the owner's learned rules mark a feature as knowingly not built, canwe reports it as "deliberately not built (decision ref)" instead of sizing it as unsized greenfield work.
why: Internal request 95, from the blind-test Q7 loss (pm/decisions.md: Nosy wrongly called deliberately-off KEP "not built yet"). canwe.mjs checks sources.json's dropped.knowingly pattern against the decision/request text before sizing (skill/tools/canwe.mjs lines 328-335, 467).

name: Nothing is written outside pm/
rule: Every script that writes output (state, drafts, the page) writes only under the product's pm/ folder; nothing is written into the product's own repo.
why: rules.md rule 4 ("The result goes to the page") and watch-rivals.mjs's own header: "Nothing is written outside pm/" (skill/tools/watch-rivals.mjs line 10).

name: Nothing external without the owner asking
rule: Push, PR, issue/comment, message, or email are never sent on the owner's behalf unless the owner explicitly asked for that specific action; PRD and issue drafts stay as files under pm/ until then.
why: rules.md, "Writing externally": "Push, opening a PR, issue/comment, message, email: never without the owner explicitly asking." nosy.mjs's own header restricts outward writes to notify (only the given webhook) and publish (only after the privacy scan).

name: No customer data or secrets read or published
rule: Before tea/spill/publish send anything outbound, the content is scanned for secrets (gitleaks-style patterns) and personal data (e-mail, phone numbers, IBANs of any country, card numbers, national ID, names it is given); either one blocks the send unless the owner passes --allow-sensitive. `nosy publish` also sends counts and structure only, never commit subjects, author names, PR or issue titles.
why: rules.md, "Positioning": "customer data, secrets, and keys are never read and never written to the page." privacy-scan.mjs's own header: exit code 1 on a high-severity finding, called by tea/spill before publishing.

name: A claim without a primary source is marked unverified
rule: Any claim not seen directly in a primary source (the product's own site, docs, changelog, or code) is labeled "(unverified)" rather than stated as fact.
why: rules.md, "Evidence": "A claim not seen in a primary source (the product's own site, docs, changelog) gets '(unverified)'." "?" means not found, and is never counted in counts.

name: Sub-agents run on cheap models
rule: Research sub-agents (e.g. rival research) run on a cheaper model (sonnet for research, haiku for review), never defaulted to the top-tier model.
why: rules.md rule 5: "Sub-agents run on cheap models (sonnet for research, haiku for review)." and "Cost": don't use a paid browser/scraper tool the user hasn't authorized.

name: Every reference in an answer is checked before it goes out
rule: Before an answer goes to the owner, every file:line in it must exist, every quote tied to a citation must be in that file word for word near that line, every commit hash must be in the repo, and every #N must match what GitHub says (exists, issue or PR, open or closed). A line that fails is fixed or dropped.
why: The owner's 20-question test (29 Sep): answers quoted English docs as Turkish sentences in quotation marks (PRODUCT.md:74), cited a handler file that doesn't exist, and reported a merged PR (#377) as "couldn't find the issue". Blind graders marked each one wrong; each is mechanically checkable.
